text:
anya: Quick sync — proposing a new "consumption" signal set for GPU pools that the runtime emits and telemetry aggregates. Goal: make routing/quota decisions (hosted vs dedicated) based on the same signals we surface in the console. Thoughts?

anya: Metrics I think we need from the runtime agent (raw):
```
gpu.sm.occupancy_fraction   # 0..1 per GPU SMs in use
gpu.sm.mem_used_bytes       # device memory used by active contexts
gpu.queue.depth            # number of waiting requests in pool queue
gpu.active_slots           # number of slots pinned/allocated
```

anya: Suggest sampling at 5s on runtime, then compute p50/p95 over 1m and 5m in telemetry. Hosted should use p95 latency/backpressure triggers; Dedicated should surface headroom and quota-consumption charts.

raj: +1 for the raw names. runtime can emit occupancy_fraction and mem_used_bytes. queue.depth is tricky because we have multi-queue per scheduler — will emit per-pool and per-queue-type (inference|priority).

raj: Implementation note: we'll tag metrics with `pool_type=hosted|dedicated`, `pool_id`, and `queue_type`. That lets console aggregate.

carmen: runtime will need an opt-in config for 5s sampling to avoid extra overhead on tiny pools. Also we should expose an event when occupancy_fraction>0.95 for >30s so routing can fast-fail or fallback.

matt: For dashboard UX I'd like both raw timeseries and a synthesized "consumption score" for each pool: e.g. 0..100 combining occupancy, mem pressure, and queue growth. Console can use that to color rows. Example prom-ish formulas: `rate(gpu.queue.depth[1m])` and `avg_over_time(gpu.sm.occupancy_fraction[5m])`.

elaine: From product POV we need clear semantics for quotas: does occupancy count against customer soft/quota usage? Or is quota only tokens/slots? We can't surprise customers with hidden "consumption" deductions.

anya: Good call. Proposal: consumption signals are only used for routing and autoscaling decisions (internal). Billing/quota stays token-based. If we expose a "consumption_estimate" to customers, it must be read-only and clearly labeled.

denise: On alerting/oncall: define signals we want for SRE alerts vs console health banners. I suggest SRE alerts on sustained p95 occupancy>0.9 or queue.depth growth > 10m slope. Console banners for sticky spikes.

metrics-bot: New metric namespace registered: `gpu.*` (source: runtime-agent v2.3). Metrics: gpu.sm.occupancy_fraction, gpu.sm.mem_used_bytes, gpu.queue.depth, gpu.active_slots.

raj: Small API debate: do we expose occupancy as fraction (0..1) or integer (#sms_busy/#sms_total) for better rollups? Fraction avoids needing two metrics, but integer pairs are more flexible. Thoughts?

carmen: I'd prefer numerator/denominator (sms_busy, sms_total) — makes correct aggregation across heterogeneous GPUs easier. We'll emit both for compatibility: occupancy_fraction (derived) + sms_busy + sms_total.

matt: Console needs consistent cardinality. Please ensure `pool_id` and `pool_type` tags are always present. Also a canonical `region` tag.\n
elaine: UX + messaging: when a customer sees a "high consumption" badge we need a tooltip: "This pool shows sustained high SM occupancy and queue pressure. Consider switching to a dedicated pool or increasing burst capacity."

anya: Next steps I propose: 1) runtime team emits numerator/denominator + mem + queue depth with tags (pool_id,pool_type,region,queue_type) by EOD next Tues; 2) telemetry team publishes aggregation queries and p50/p95 calculations; 3) console team prototypes a per-pool consumption score visualization and health banners. Who owns step 2?

denise: SRE will take step 2 (aggregation and alert thresholds) but will coordinate with telemetry infra for retention and downsampling.

raj: Will start runtime PR for metric emission. Will also add an opt-in release flag.

carmen: We'll include the event (occupancy>0.95 for 30s) as part of the metrics stream and emit a structured event to the control plane.

matt: I'll make a lightweight mockup for the console table and share in #product-ux tomorrow.

elaine: I'll draft the customer-facing tooltip and doc blurb once Matt's mock is up.

anya: Thanks all — can we reconvene next Wed to review telemetry queries + mockups? :calendar: :eyes:

raj: Works for me.

carmen: 👍

denise: I'll put a stub runbook for oncall actions when the new alerts fire.

metrics-bot: metrics agent v2.3 deployed to staging at 2026-03-18T14:12:07Z

anya: Great, I'll follow up with a short RFC summarizing the agreed metric names and tags.

matt: FYI — linking to similar dashboard patterns: https://redwood.internal/docs/pools/consumption-patterns :thumbsup:

anya: end"
